newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan gov't to transfer equity for reinvestment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gov't to transfer equity for reinvestment.

text.p: Taiwan's government said on Wednesday it would transfer its equity in local electronic firms from the economics ministry to a cabinet venture capital fund for reinvestment in the high-technology industry.

The cabinet's economic policymaking arm said transfer of an estimated T$40 billion in high-tech shares would give the state new financial flexibility, enabling it to reinvest profits rather than merely parking them in the treasury.

"The economics ministry has to turn all its stock profits over to the state treasury, while the cabinet's Development Fund operates like any other venture capital firm," Wu Chung-yin, a director for the Council for Economic Planning and Development, said by telephone.
"The transfer will afford the government more freedom to re-invest money made from stocks," Wu said.
Wu said the Development Fund would place its newly obtained shares in a special fund concentrating on investments in high-tech sector, increasingly seen as the key to Taiwan's economic future.

The ministry said it now holds some T$40 billion worth of electronic shares, including 138 million shares worth T$12 billion in listed United Microelectronics, Taiwan's second largest computer chipmaker.
The exact value fluctuates daily according to transactions in the stock market, a ministry spokeswoman said.
The ministry has not devised a timetable for the planned stock transfer, she said. "We are currently working on a schedule," she said without elaborating.

Many private analysts view Taiwan's electronic industry -- which fields some of the world's leading semiconductor and computer firms -- as having the most promising outlook out of all the island's economic sectors.
